analysis.title: UBS 3Q energy review, US strikes Qeshm + Energy Daily 03/11/26
key_insights: Brent fell about 12% from last Friday's high to yesterday's intraday low and reversed slightly this morning. The UBS specialist sales author argues optimism on US-Iran diplomacy is not entirely justified because Iran's core demands are unchanged and the US has little incentive to concede more after the midterms.
The US struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz yesterday. The author does not read it as a precursor to renewed diplomacy. Hormuz flows have ticked up slightly in recent days.
Iran's Supreme Leader authorised President Pezeshkian to seek a diplomatic solution. The US and Iran are reportedly reviewing proposals from Qatari mediators.

UBS EU integrated energy 3Q review shows an average 7% beat against estimates that had risen about 15% between trading updates and results. It is the second consecutive quarter in which every company beat consensus.
The EU integrated group is pricing in about $74/b Brent on a normalised refining margin, perhaps mid-high $60s on a less conservative refining margin than the $10.3/b UBS uses for 2027.
Sector sentiment is very sensitive to an oil correction, but positioning and relative valuation should support EU integrateds even if a correction is sustained.
BP is the most interesting EU integrated on catalyst and valuation. Shell is the most crowded long for now, given its balance sheet and a buyback surprise announced with 3Q results.

Nasdaq fell 1.4% and is in correction territory, with futures trading through Friday's lows. Damage was concentrated in the AI complex (Neoclouds -8%, Memory -5%, Momentum -4.7%), while Quality (+2.4%) and Staples/Discretionary (+1.5-2.5%) absorbed flows.
META ($20bn debt) and ORCL ($20bn equity plus debt) are both tapping funding markets. AAPL fell about 3% after hours on a soft services growth guide.

Equities took no comfort from crude finishing down by double digits. KOSPI and TAIEX fell 3-4%. China outperformed marginally on a regulator support package including a third SFISF operation of more than 100bn CNY.

UBS Derivatives Strategy estimates Risk Control funds turn to buyers after two days of heavy selling, and CTA supply is largely complete. Retail, foreign investors and multi-asset managers have bought the dip for three sessions.

Democrats enter US midterm election day with an 8-9pt generic-ballot advantage and are priced at roughly 80-90% to win the House and 60-67% to win the Senate. UBS Research says a blue sweep looks largely priced and would produce modest curve flattening. A Republican sweep is the bigger market risk and could prompt a sharp long-end sell-off.
After the election, Treasury quarterly refunding keeps risks biased toward higher long-end yields and renewed curve steepening.
Shell agreed to sell its 16.67% non-operated stake in North West Shelf to XRG for a base $1.45bn plus a milestone-linked contingent payment. Closing is expected in 2027.

Saudi Aramco 3Q26 adjusted net income of $31.2bn was 2% above company-compiled consensus of $30.7bn. Capex of $10.5bn was 20% below consensus. Free cash flow of $28.2bn was 2% above consensus. Gearing fell to 5.5%.
Diamondback Energy raised its 2026 production outlook to about 1.015 million boepd and capex to $3.95-4.00bn. Q3 Brent averaged $89.27/bbl, 31% above a year earlier.
Dubai nearest timespread is in contango, with the November contract about $2/bbl below December, signalling near-term supply outpacing demand for the first time since July.
US LNG exports reached the second-highest monthly level on record in October. Exports to Europe were 6.89 million tonnes. TTF and JKM both averaged about $28/MMBtu.

market_movers.rationale: UBS specialist sales calls BP the most interesting EU integrated on catalyst and valuation. Research flags BP as one of the most supportive 3Q updates.
Strong balance sheet and a buyback surprise with 3Q results, but it is described as the most crowded long in the space for now.
UBS research reiterates Buy and raises PT after call takeaways and estimate changes. The note gives no PT figure.
UBS research adjusts estimates and raises PT after call takeaways. The note gives no PT figure or rating.
UBS views the 3Q update as positive with good quarterly results and updates on near and long-term initiatives.
3Q EBITDAX and capex beats, and a royalties unit IPO filing is a positive step to unlock value.
3Q26 earnings beat and an MOU with Bloom Energy to advance 1GW or more of decarbonized power in California.
Agreements to acquire a 30% operated interest in two Malaysian gas fields, called a small positive. The fields could add 11-17% of the extra supply needed for its 2030-35 growth.
Plaquemines LNG Phase 1 reached commercial operations just over 53 months after FID, which should raise confidence in on-schedule execution.

sector_views.rationale: Positioning and attractive relative valuation should support the group even in a sustained oil correction. The group prices about $74/b Brent.
Tech is the overhang on equities. The AI complex led the selloff and Nasdaq is in correction territory.

earnings_insights: EU integrated energy 3Q26 (UBS Research): average 7% beat against estimates that had risen about 15% between trading updates and results. Every company beat consensus for the second consecutive quarter. Eni and BP gave the most supportive updates.

Saudi Aramco 3Q26 (reported): adjusted net income pre-minorities $31.2bn vs company-compiled consensus $30.7bn (UBSe $30.9bn). CFO $38.7bn vs VA consensus $40.7bn (UBSe $39.3bn), with the gap entirely working capital. CFFO ex-WC $37.7bn vs consensus $37.3bn. Capex $10.5bn vs consensus and UBSe $13.1bn. FCF $28.2bn vs consensus $27.6bn (UBSe $26.1bn).
Diamondback Energy 3Q26 (reported): profit beat expectations per Reuters. 2026 output outlook raised to about 1.015 million boepd, from over 1 million. 2026 capex guided to $3.95-4.00bn from $3.9bn.
Crescent Energy 3Q26 (reported): EBITDAX and capex beats per UBS Research, plus a confidential IPO filing for Crescent Royalties.
California Resources 3Q26 (reported): earnings beat per UBS Research.
Petronet LNG Q2FY27 (reported): EBITDA of Rs16.6bn was 10% above consensus, possibly aided by inventory and trading gains. Total volumes 4.53mmt.
S-Oil 3Q26 (reported): operating profit rose to W1.41tn on refining and record lube. The 4Q outlook remains tight.
ENN Natural Gas 9M26 (reported): operating profit of Rmb3.7bn, likely to improve sequentially in Q4 2026.
AAPL (reported by trading desk): fell about 3% after hours on a soft services growth guide.

risk_factors: Renewed US-Iran escalation or failed diplomacy keeps oil volatile, and sector sentiment is very sensitive to an oil correction.
A Republican sweep in the midterms could cause a sharp long-end sell-off.
Treasury quarterly refunding biases risk toward higher long-end yields and curve steepening.
Funding supply from META and ORCL debt and equity issuance at a weak point for sentiment.
Rotation out of AI and momentum names continues to hit tech.
Europe enters winter with lower gas storage, and TotalEnergies' CEO says it will pay more for supply.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq is in correction territory after a 1.4% drop, and futures trade through Friday's lows.
UBS Derivatives Strategy estimates Risk Control funds turn to buyers after two days of heavy selling. CTA supply is largely complete with limited incremental impact.
Retail, foreign investors and multi-asset managers have bought the dip over the past three sessions.
Shell is described as the most crowded long among EU integrated energy names.
Monday UBS flow was balanced at 51/49, with participation about 40% above the YTD average.
geopolitical: US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.
Iran's Supreme Leader authorised President Pezeshkian to seek a diplomatic solution, and the US and Iran are reviewing proposals from Qatari mediators.
The US-Israeli war with Iran, which began at the end of February, is in its eighth month and has disrupted energy supplies. Hormuz flows have ticked up recently.
Trump signalled a deal could be struck ahead of the midterms, though reports of further strikes continue.
US midterm elections are underway, with the last poll closing in Alaska at 06:00 GMT on Wednesday 4 November.
Russian air strike on a humanitarian aid center in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, killed at least 24 people.
QatarEnergy extended force majeure on LNG supplies until the end of the year.
The UAE left OPEC in April and says its oil exports have risen despite the war.
Canada fast-tracked review of the Pacific Link oil pipeline, and Cheam First Nation filed a Federal Court challenge.

tension_points.bull_case: Iran's Supreme Leader authorised talks, the US and Iran are reviewing Qatari proposals, Trump signalled a deal before the midterms, and Hormuz flows are rising. Brent fell about 12% from Friday's high.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran's core demands are unchanged, the US has little incentive to concede more after the midterms, and the US struck Qeshm Island yesterday. Further strikes are reported.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US concession or announced deal that visibly renews peace talks would undermine the bearish read. Continued strikes or stalled talks would support it.

tension_points.bull_case: Every company beat consensus for the second quarter running, and the group prices only about $74/b Brent, with positioning and valuation providing support.
tension_points.bear_case: The bar is high after estimates rose about 15%, and sentiment is very sensitive to an oil correction. Shell is the most crowded long.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained oil correction below the Brent level the group prices, about $74/b, would test the support argument.
